channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Nunes Marques vota contra ação do PT para aumentar fundo eleitoral da sigla
item.description: TSE President Kássio Nunes Marques voted against a PT action seeking to increase the party's share of the electoral fund, but the judgment was suspended after a request for review by Minister Estela Aranha. The partial decision comes as the PT seeks to expand its financial resources for the 2026 election campaign.

item.title: Fazenda libera empréstimo do Banco do Brasil para São Paulo após ação de Tarcísio no STF
item.description: The Brazilian Ministry of Finance authorized a federal guarantee for a Banco do Brasil loan to São Paulo just hours after Governor Tarcísio de Freitas filed a lawsuit at the STF accusing the Lula administration of delaying the approval. The move responds to the state’s claim that federal inaction was jeopardizing investments. The authorization was issued on August 13, 2026, at 10:02 AM.

item.title: Ministros do TSE destacam que PL não pode usar Bolsonaro em campanha seja qual for resultado sobre uso de IA
item.description: TSE ministers state that the PL and Flávio Bolsonaro cannot use images or videos of former President Jair Bolsonaro in their campaign, regardless of the TSE's ruling on AI use in elections, due to an STF ban preventing him from making political-electoral statements. The PGR backed this stance, advocating for maintaining prohibitions on deepfakes and politically motivated visits involving Bolsonaro. TSE President Minister Nunes Marques is expected to propose a fine against Flávio Bolsonaro for disseminating an AI-generated video of his father urging votes during the convention that formalized his candidacy.

item.title: O milionário patrimônio de Edmundo ‘animal’, candidato a deputado federal pelo Rio
item.description: Former footballer Edmundo, running for federal deputy under the PSDB in Rio de Janeiro, declared R$16.059.865,50 in assets to the Electoral Justice, including real estate, investments, a luxury vehicle, and financial applications. His wealth reflects his successful football career, with stints at Vasco, Flamengo, and the Brazilian National Team, as well as post-retirement business activities.

item.title: Haddad declara R$ 861 mil em bens ao TSE
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT), candidate for governor of São Paulo, declared total assets of R$ 861,217.25 to the TSE, according to a post by O Antagonista. The assets include R$ 435,300 in financial investments, R$ 140,000 in company stocks, and a 26% stake in a property in the Planalto Paulista neighborhood valued at R$ 183,000.

item.title: Depois de mais uma bola fora de Eduardo, Flávio Bolsonaro faz promessa sobre vacinas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) proposes expanding national vaccine production and improving the SUS through AI and a unique electronic health record tied to CPF, aiming to distance himself from his brother Eduardo’s anti-vaccine activism in the U.S. The move comes amid a measles outbreak in São Paulo and criticism of Eduardo’s stance, which Flávio views as damaging to the family’s image. The plan also includes digitizing public services and integrating SUS with INSS.

item.title: Cobertor curto: governo tira R$ 500 milhões do Minha Casa para reforçar Auxílio Gás
item.description: The Lula government transferred R$ 500 million from the Residential Leasing Fund (FAR), used in the Minha Casa, Minha Vida program, to strengthen the Auxílio Gás and other social assistance actions. This move occurs in a context of budget adjustment, where the government seeks to preserve income transfer programs ahead of the 2026 elections, even as it reduces investment in social housing. The Planning Ministry’s portaria confirms the reallocation, though it has not specified how many homes will no longer be financed.

item.title: O argumento do PT ao TSE contra vídeo de Bolsonaro gerado por IA
item.description: The PT argued before the TSE that the use of an AI-generated video of Jair Bolsonaro in Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign is irregular, as the ban on synthetic content since 2024 is objective and does not require proof of actual harm, even with an AI disclaimer. The party maintains that simulating real identities via avatars or chatbots is prohibited regardless of tone or technical quality. The TSE will rule on whether the video's use was permissible despite the AI disclosure.

item.title: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro e outros candidatos a presidente inauguram campanha neste domingo com atos pelo Brasil; veja onde será cada um
item.description: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Renan Santos, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema launch their presidential campaigns this Sunday, August 16, with events in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, and Minas Gerais. Lula chose Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo to symbolize his political origins in the ABC labor movement, while Flávio Bolsonaro will hold a truck convoy in Rio de Janeiro. Caiado and Zema opted for events in their home states of Goiás and Minas Gerais, respectively.

item.title: O decreto de Lula que permitirá você escolher sua fornecedora de energia elétrica
item.description: President Lula signed a decree opening the free electricity market to low-voltage consumers, allowing commercial and industrial establishments to choose their supplier starting November 2027 and residential consumers from 2028. The measure aims to stimulate competition, reduce electricity bills by up to 20%, and establishes rules for the Free Contracting Environment (ACL) and the Supplier of Last Resort (SUI), with the latter’s responsibility remaining with distributors until 2030.

item.title: A enganação dos Bolsonaros fakes e a farsa do currículo de Flávio
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry is investigating at least 17 fake candidacies using the Bolsonaro surname in São Paulo, with no civil registry or familial ties to the Bolsonaro family, aimed at misleading conservative voters. Noblat’s program also revealed that Flávio Bolsonaro maintained a false postgraduate degree in Political Sciences on his official Senate and Rio de Janeiro Assembly profiles for years, blamed by his staff on 'Wikipedia errors'. Furthermore, the plan to hold a motorcycle rally to Juiz de Fora to exploit the 2018 stabbing of Jair Bolsonaro was criticized as opportunistic.

item.title: Contra "efeito Tebet", PP quer aproximação de Derrite com prefeitos
item.description: The Progressistas (PP) is urging Senate candidate Guilherme Derrite to focus on municipalism and the countryside of São Paulo to counter the 'Tebet effect,' as he is seen as a niche candidate known mainly in the metropolitan area and on social media. There is concern that the interior will vote for the André do Prado (PL) and Simone Tebet (PSB) ticket, jeopardizing his chances. Derrite has increased his presence in the interior, holding events in Botucatu, São Carlos, São Sebastião, and Itapetininga, with planned visits to Itapeva and Marília, always alongside André do Prado and with the support of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas.

item.title: Currículo anabolizado dá a Flávio pós-graduação em mentirologia
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro and a pre-candidate for the PL in the 2026 presidential race, was accused of falsely listing a postgraduate degree in Political Science on his resume — a degree he never completed. The misleading information appeared on the Alerj website, the Senate portal, and his LinkedIn profile, sparking criticism for inflating his academic credentials. The incident has been dubbed an 'anabolized resume' and raised concerns about his credibility.

item.title: TSE avalia nesta quinta-feira proibição do uso de deepfakes na campanha eleitoral
item.description: The TSE is set to evaluate on Thursday a definitive ban on the use of deepfakes in electoral campaigns, following a case involving an AI-generated video of former President Jair Bolsonaro shown at the PL party convention. The ruling could establish precedent for the 2026 elections, as current resolutions already prohibit deepfakes that benefit or harm candidates, but ministers debate whether minor image or voice corrections should also be banned. The defense claims the video was labeled as AI and thus not deceptive, while the TSE favors a broad ban to avoid excessive judicialization.

item.title: A aposta de Lula em podcasts para alcançar geração Z e apresentar lado ‘gente da gente’
item.description: President Lula plans to increase his appearances on podcasts and videocasts during the 2026 campaign to reach Generation Z, presenting a more relatable, everyday side of his life distant from formal politics. The strategy, according to PT communications secretary Éden Valadares, aims to connect with voters who only know Lula as an institutional figure, showcasing the 'Lula, just like us'.

item.title: Flávio compartilha diplomas após “equívoco” no currículo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) shared images of his diplomas after UFRJ stated there is no record of his course completion, in response to academic background scrutiny. The move aims to clarify doubts about his education following the 'error' pointed out by the university. This occurs amid his 2026 presidential pre-campaign.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro publica diplomas de graduação, MBA e especialização após revelação sobre curso de pós que ele não fez
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro published his academic diplomas after being exposed for falsely claiming a postgraduate degree in Political Sciences from UFRJ in his official profiles. He denied completing the course and attributed the error to 'mistakes' possibly copied from sources like Wikipedia. The incident drew criticism from political opponents who questioned the accuracy of his academic credentials in campaign and institutional materials.

item.title: Nem Lula nem Flávio Bolsonaro fazem os olhos da classe C brilhar, diz Renato Meirelles
item.description: Renato Meirelles states that neither Lula nor Flávio Bolsonaro manage to inspire hope in Brazil's C class, as neither understands that work is no longer synonymous with formal employment. Despite lingering gratitude for past improvements under Lula's government, the C class lacks a vision for a better future, with many losing purchasing power and fearing violence. Meirelles emphasizes that income, work, consumption, religion, and daily experiences weigh more on voting decisions than traditional political analysis.

item.title: As propostas de Flávio Bolsonaro para mudar o SUS
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposes a unique electronic health record linked to the CPF to integrate public and private health services, aiming to reduce bureaucracy and prevent duplicate exams. His plan also includes modernizing federal university hospitals, delivering medication at home for vulnerable groups, correcting the SUS table, expanding the Family Health Strategy, and digitizing the INSS to reduce waiting times for benefits.

item.title: Jingle, slogan e relatos de beneficiários de programas sociais: como será o ato de Lula no ABC
item.description: Lula is preparing a mega-event to launch his re-election campaign in São Bernardo do Campo (SP) on Sunday, August 16, featuring a new jingle, the slogan 'Brazil ready for more', and testimonials from beneficiaries of social programs. The event will be more streamlined than the August 2 convention, with greater space for women to speak and expected attendance from allies across the country. The campaign also plans a remake of the 'Lula Lá' jingle and distribution of WhatsApp stickers.

item.title: Projeto dos combustíveis e a economia política do possível (e cobrado) ajuste fiscal de 2027
item.description: The negotiations surrounding the fuel bill (PLP 114) serve as a key indicator of the political economy behind a potential fiscal adjustment in 2027, particularly if President Lula is re-elected. The bill reflects tensions between the need for revenue and sectoral resistance, suggesting future fiscal measures will be negotiated with powerful interests rather than imposed unilaterally. The subscriber-only article implies that the 2027 fiscal adjustment will be 'charged' — meaning shaped by pressures and bargains, not technocratic decree.

item.title: Flávio ou Michelle?
item.description: A poll of 604 readers asked who came out better in the feud between Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle Bolsonaro. The majority (56.8%) said neither came out well, while Michelle was chosen by 37.6% and Flávio by only 5.6%. The result suggests a negative or indifferent public perception of the confrontation between the two.

item.title: A nova variável eleitoral
item.description: Major centrist parties, including MDB, Republicanos, Podemos, and the União Progressista federation (União Brasil and PP), are avoiding taking sides in the 2026 presidential race to preserve their state structures and focus on building parliamentary benches. This decision, beyond being pragmatic, is now being shaped by legal risks stemming from STF rulings on budgetary amendments, particularly ADPF 854/DF, which challenge the legitimacy of party leaders directing funds without a mandate. The new electoral variable in 2026 is thus the assessment of legal risk tied to presidential alliances.

item.title: Chapéu usado por Lula (PT) pode levar até seis meses para ser feito; conheça a história do Panamá
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wears a Panama hat for protection following skin cancer surgery on his scalp. Made from Ecuadorian toquilla straw, the hat takes between two days and six months to craft manually, despite its name originating during the Panama Canal construction. The hat also appears in Lula’s official photo for the 2026 elections registered with the TSE.

item.title: Candidatura de Salles ao Senado racha direita em SP e expõe tensão com aliado de Tarcísio
item.description: Ricardo Salles's (Novo) independent Senate bid in São Paulo is causing fractures on the right, as he criticizes André do Prado (PL) for not being sufficiently Bolsonarist. Salles and Prado are technically tied in polls, trailing left and center candidates, while Guilherme Derrite (PP), an ally of Tarcísio de Freitas, refrained from attacking Salles and urged right-wing unity. Prado's absence at events featuring Tarcísio and Flávio Bolsonaro underscored the growing rift within the governing coalition.

item.title: Lula sem 'frente ampla' e Flávio isolado: por que líderes nas pesquisas não têm mais apoio político?
item.description: Although Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead in the polls for the 2026 presidential race, they struggle to build broad party alliances, unlike in 2022. This reflects a structural shift in Brazilian politics, where parties now prioritize congressional contests to control parliamentary amendments (R$ 61 billion in 2026) and negotiate post-election support, making presidential coalitions rare — a phenomenon not seen since 1989. The polarization between lulismo and bolsonarismo also prevents the Centrão from forming stable alliances with either pole, leaving most candidates to run solely under their own party banners.

item.title: IA de Bolsonaro: sem consenso, TSE se reúne para discutir deepfake
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) is meeting to discuss the use of deepfakes in the 2026 elections following a challenge to an AI-generated avatar of Jair Bolsonaro used by Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign. While the court is divided, President Kassio Nunes Marques appears inclined toward a lenient stance and will set a date for the avatar’s trial. The PT and Brazil of Hope Federation claim the video constitutes premature electoral propaganda and illegal AI use, demanding its removal, a fine of R$ 30,000 per publication, and a ban on future dissemination.

item.title: Lula e Alcolumbre retomam relação na véspera da eleição e de olho em 2027
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre resumed dialogue in a meeting at the Palácio da Alvorada, after months of tension, aiming to unblock government agendas in the Senate ahead of the October elections. The meeting, described as relaxed by Minister José Guimarães, included Senate Government Leader Teresa Leitão and followed a prior dinner at the residence of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The move seeks to strengthen political coordination for the remainder of the electoral year and beyond, with an eye on 2027.

item.title: Sob pressão de China e UE, Brasil mira novos mercados para carne
item.description: Brazil is seeking new markets for its beef exports amid restrictions imposed by China and the European Union, which threaten to significantly reduce external sales. The Lula government is prioritizing negotiations with Japan, South Korea, and Canada to diversify destinations and mitigate the impacts of Chinese quotas and the EU ban, set to take effect on September 3 unless reversed.

item.title: Plano de Tarcísio promete "turbinar" Tabela SUS Paulista e Butantan
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' re-election plan proposes expanding the São Paulo SUS Table to include municipal hospitals, renaming it SUS Paulista Municípios, and investing around R$ 4 billion in the Butantan Institute to boost vaccine and drug production. The program has already allocated R$ 11 billion to philanthropic hospitals since 2023, paying R$ 2,200 per normal birth versus R$ 443 from the federal government. Health was deemed a 'weak point' of the administration, with internal criticism directed at Health Secretary Eleuses Paiva, whose continuation in office is uncertain if the governor is re-elected.

item.title: Kassab prepara coquetel para incentivar voto “Carcísio” no agro de SP
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD and vice-presidential candidate, is hosting a cocktail at the Santos Yacht Club for São Paulo agribusiness leaders to promote Ronaldo Caiado, governor of Goiás, as a political alternative. The event supports the so-called 'Carcísio' vote — a Caiado-Tarcísio alliance aimed at defeating Lula in a potential runoff — though some agribusiness figures remain loyal to Flávio Bolsonaro, creating internal tension within the conservative bloc.

item.title: Eleições 2026: por que candidatos ainda não podem pedir votos?
item.description: The 2026 elections begin on October 4, but candidates may only request votes starting August 16, per a 2019 TSE resolution. Before that date, they can participate in interviews, debates, and share policy views, but any explicit or implicit vote solicitation constitutes illegal early campaigning, punishable by fines of R$5,000 to R$25,000 or content removal. The rule resurfaced in public debate after Lourdes Melo (PCO-PI) ironically said, 'Do not vote for me'.

item.title: Reaproximação com Alcolumbre ainda não destravou pautas de Lula
item.description: The rapprochement between Lula and Alcolumbre enabled the swift approval of the Fuel PLP, but did not advance the PECs on Public Security and the 6×1 workweek, both still awaiting Senate referral since March and May. The government is frustrated by the lack of a voting schedule, particularly for the 40-hour workweek PEC, a key re-election pledge.

item.title: Candidatos voltam às origens para lançar campanhas presidenciais
item.description: The main presidential candidates for the 2026 Brazilian elections launched their campaigns in symbolic locations tied to their political origins. Lula kicked off his re-election bid in São Bernardo do Campo, while Flávio Bolsonaro chose Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro. Other candidates, including Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, and Renan Santos, also returned to their political strongholds to begin the race.

item.title: Revés judicial do governo em mudança no Bolsa Família deve diminuir economia inicialmente prevista no orçamento em 2027
item.description: A judicial setback regarding Bolsa Família rules may reduce the savings initially projected for 2027, estimated at 25 billion reais, challenging the government’s fiscal targets. However, the administration secured a win by approving expense containment triggers in the complementary bill for fuel tax exemption, which could be applied in 2025 to partially offset the impact. The judicial decision directly affects the spending review conducted throughout Lula’s third term.

item.title: Alexandre de Moraes fragiliza democracia ao violar sigilo da fonte de jornalista
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes is accused of weakening democracy by violating the confidentiality of a journalist's source, a right protected as a constitutional clause in Brazil. The article argues that source confidentiality is crucial for investigations exposing corruption and abuse of power, such as the Mensalão, Operation Car Wash, and other scandals, and that its breach undermines public interest reporting. The content is presented as subscriber-only, requiring registration for full access.

item.title: Como será a campanha? O que a pesquisa indicou? Colunistas do GLOBO respondem na nova newsletter 'A pergunta da semana'
item.description: O GLOBO launched the 'Question of the Week' newsletter to analyze the 2026 election, starting with the inquiry about the truce between Flávio Bolsonaro and Michelle. The initiative is part of a broader package of innovations that includes other newsletters, live sessions, in-depth reports, and the 'Fora da bolha' videocast, focusing on topics such as economy, violence, and religion in the campaign.

item.title: Implante de cabelo, perda de peso e renovação do guarda-roupa: candidatos apostam em mudanças de visual antes da eleição
item.description: Brazilian political candidates and leaders, including Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Caiado, Tarcísio, and Renan Santos, are investing in visual transformations — such as hair implants, weight loss, and wardrobe updates — to convey youth, vitality, and closeness to voters ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Evento em estádio, ato na praia, carreata e até show de violão: como será o primeiro dia de campanha dos presidenciáveis
item.description: Presidential candidates have defined their campaign launch events for Sunday: Lula at Vila Euclides Stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, Flávio Bolsonaro at Copacabana Beach, Ronaldo Caiado in a motorcade through Goiás interior, Romeu Zema in Montes Claros (MG), and Renan Santos (Missão) without a disclosed location. The choices reflect strategies to mobilize grassroots support, evoke historic social struggles, and test electoral reach.

item.title: Centrão se mantém neutro na maioria dos estados e se distancia de PT e PL até mesmo em colégios-chave
item.description: State directories of the União Brasil-PP and Republicanos parties, authorized by national leadership to support either PT or PL, chose neutrality in most states, avoiding alignment with Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro. While 25 state commands remained neutral, 16 leaned toward Bolsonaro’s son and 11 toward the PT, reflecting a broader strategy of distancing from the polarized presidential race.

item.title: Roteiros reescritos por marqueteiro, queixas de candidatos e Arthur Lira: os bastidores da ‘rave de gravações’ de Flávio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign conducted a two-day video recording operation with 47 Senate candidates in Brasília, dubbed the 'rave of recordings,' with scripts revised by strategist Duda Lima. The marathon caused complaints from candidates like Coronel Hélio (RN), who arrived first but was delayed to the second day, missing personal commitments. Arthur Lira (PP-AL) visited the campaign's legal headquarters during the event, underscoring the political mobilization around Flávio's strategy to bolster a pro-government Senate bloc to support his presidential bid.

item.title: Abordagem da PM acirra ânimos entre Haddad e Tarcísio
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) accused the Military Police of an intimidating approach against his driver after leaving his residence in São Paulo’s southern zone, claiming the vehicle was spotlighted and followed for 40 minutes by officers armed with rifles. Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) ordered an investigation through the SSP, whose secretary contacted Haddad to gather details, stating the PM was pursuing a glass-breaking gang. The allegation was made during an interview after an OAB-SP forum, with Haddad suggesting the incident reflects political use of public security.

item.title: Ministros do TSE devem debater veto amplo a deepfakes na campanha eleitoral e discutir punição para caso Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: TSE ministers are set to discuss in a closed meeting the broadening of a ban on deepfakes in electoral campaigns for 2026, regardless of whether the content benefits or harms candidates, including avatars and manipulations with apparent consent. The discussion stems from a PT representation against an AI-generated video showing Jair Bolsonaro supporting Flávio Bolsonaro, seen as the first major test of the TSE’s AI rules for the 2026 elections. The case is expected to result in a fine, not harsher sanctions, with severe penalties reserved for repeat offenses or abuse.

item.title: Plano de Flávio propõe impedir parentes de ministros de advogar no STF
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's government plan proposes banning relatives up to the third degree of STF and other superior court ministers from practicing law before the Supreme Court, expanding the current rule that only disqualifies judges from hearing cases involving their relatives. The plan also seeks to limit monocratic decisions at the STF, favor collegial rulings, presume the constitutionality of legislative processes, and remove the Court's criminal jurisdiction, restricting it to its original constitutional duties.

item.title: O homem por trás da crise entre Brasil e Estados Unidos - O Assunto #1782
item.description: The U.S. State Department's video asserting American dominance in the Americas, invoking the Monroe Doctrine, sparked a diplomatic crisis with Brazil, including the revocation of the visa of Brazilian ambassador Maria Luísa Viotti. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State and Trump's national security advisor, is portrayed as an ideological Republican who has declared 'this is our hemisphere' and is viewed as hostile to the Lula government. Political scientist Carlos Gustavo Poggio warns of the risk of Rubio's interference in Brazil's October 2026 elections.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Guia do Eleitor
item.description: The voter guide for the 2026 elections outlines the first round on October 4, with voting from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Brasília time nationwide. It details ID requirements (including e-Title), how to find polling places, rules on prohibited items like phones in voting booths, absentee and justified voting, penalties for not voting, and procedures to report electoral irregularities. It also covers dress code, cellphone use, and electoral crime prevention.

item.title: Flávio apresentará plano de governo em live nesta quinta; programa prevê dobrar verba para segurança e novo ministério
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro will unveil his government plan 'For Brazil to Overcome Backwardness' in a Thursday live stream, proposing to at least double federal investments in public security, create a Ministry of Public Security, and deploy a national facial recognition system called 'Muralha Brasileira'. The plan also includes reducing the number of ministries, administrative reform, and controversial measures such as lowering the age of criminal responsibility and chemical castration for child abusers and rapists.

item.title: Ministros do TSE se reúnem nesta quinta e avaliam proibição do uso de deepfake na campanha eleitoral
item.description: TSE ministers are meeting this Thursday to discuss a potential ban on deepfake use in the 2026 electoral campaigns, weighing whether the prohibition should be absolute or limited to cases of voter deception or candidate harm. The meeting follows a PT-led action against an AI-generated video of former President Jair Bolsonaro shown at the convention that nominated Flávio Bolsonaro as the PL’s presidential candidate. The goal is to prevent a flood of legal challenges and establish clear penalties, ranging from fines and warnings to stricter sanctions for repeat offenders.

item.title: Após inflar currículo com pós-graduação inexistente, Flávio compartilha diplomas e cita 'anos de estudo e dedicação'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro shared diplomas for a law degree, public policies specialization, and an MBA in entrepreneurship after his claimed postgraduate degree in Political Sciences at UFRJ was debunked by the university. His campaign confirmed the UFRJ qualification does not exist in his records, attributing the error to sources like Wikipedia, and said corrections have been requested. He emphasized his years of study and dedication, pledging to expand access to qualification if elected president.

item.title: Caiado diz que currículo de Flávio Bolsonaro é a certidão de nascimento
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) resume, claiming it amounts only to a birth certificate after UFRJ denied the senator completed a postgraduate degree in Political Sciences. Caiado also accused Flávio and Lula of being 'cowards and yellow-bellied' if they avoid presidential debates, intensifying his attacks on the Bolsonaro family.
